title: Sprint-end debrief: rollback criteria and mitigation checklist
content:
Sprint-end debrief — Release Train 2026.03 (notes, criteria, and concrete mitigation checklist)

Meeting context:
- Date: 2026-03-09
- Attendees: Marcus Liu (owner), Elena Park (release lead), Sofia Torres (QA), Ravi Menon (infra), Priya Nandakumar (SRE/Oncall), James O'Connor (platform eng)
- Goal: capture precise rollback criteria used this sprint, codify a short mitigation checklist for hotfix escalation, and note automation/code changes required before next release window.

Summary of issues observed during canary and early ramp
1) 1.8% 5xx spike on model-serving path after model-variant swap at t+12m. Spike correlated with increased median server-side decode latency (p50 -> p90 regressed by ~220ms). No customer-visible errors recorded in hosted tier but latency SLO creep observed for a small set of routes.
2) Cache invalidation race on prefix cache after KV-layout change: cache churn caused increased token-generation CPU and a downstream queueing effect on dedicated pools.
3) Two minor rollout script failures (one incorrect tag filter in deploy job) caused a missed canary step and required manual verification.
4) Post-deploy smoke test flake on reranking endpoint under synthetic load (repro across two instances) — traced to a quantized kernel scheduling edge-case on a subset of GPU types.

Decisions taken in the meeting
- Immediate: revert the model-variant swap on hosted canary until the quantized kernel fix lands (manual rollback triggered at 09:35, restored stable variant).
- Short term: apply a temporary circuit-breaker threshold for the affected reranking route to reduce concurrency by 30% while fix is validated (PR queued: GITHUB-PR-1298).
- Mid term: add a preflight check to catch tag-filter regressions in deploy scripts and block merges until preflight passes.

Explicit rollback criteria (codified) — these are now the canonical gate per release-engineering policy:
A rollback (automated or manual) MUST be initiated if any one of the following is observed during canary or ramp: 
- Error-rate threshold breached: sustained increase of 5xx errors > 1% absolute over baseline for 5 minutes, or >2% for 1 minute (route-level).
- Latency SLO breach: p95 latency increased by >= 30% vs canary baseline for 5 minutes AND user-facing request timeout risk exists.
- Data integrity risk: any client-visible corruption or malformed outputs (e.g., truncated structured responses, missing required fields).
- Resource exhaustion: sustained GPU memory pressure > 90% or CPU load causing service threads to be starved for > 3 minutes.
- Critical infra regression: control-plane failures preventing safe roll-forward (e.g., deploy job failures that skip canary).

Escalation path when rollback criteria met:
1) Oncall (Priya) pauses traffic ramp and notifies release lead in #release-ops.
2) Release lead (Elena) assesses immediate impact and authorizes rollback.
3) Infra (Ravi) initiates capacity drain for affected pool and triggers revert playbook (CONFLUENCE-Release-Runbook -> rollback checklist).
4) Communications: Post to status.redwood.com if customer impact > C2; update internal incident channel INC-2026-03-08-01.

Mitigation checklist (short form) — to be run by infra + oncall while rollback/patch is in progress:
- [ ] Pin routing to stable model variant (feature-flag toggle: model-routing.stable=true).
- [ ] Disable experimental quantized kernels via runtime flag on affected GPU family.
- [ ] Increase canary observation window by 10 minutes for model-serving path (config: release.ramp.canary_window_override).
- [ ] Re-run smoke suite with focused load on reranking/embedding endpoints (QA note: use test-profile: rerank-heavy-v2).
- [ ] Check KV prefix-caching metrics: cache hit rate, eviction rate, and time-to-first-fetch after change.
- [ ] If resource pressure observed, autoscale dedicated pool by +15% immediate burst and notify capacity owners.
- [ ] Ensure deploy job preflight script is executed locally and in CI (add gating check: deploy/preflight -> JIRA-4821).

Postmortem action items (owners and rough ETA)
- A1: Fix quantized kernel scheduling edge-case and add unit tests for scheduling handoff on GPU family b3. Owner: Elena Park. ETA: 2026-03-19.
- A2: Harden prefix-cache invalidation logic with backoff and stronger ordering guarantees; add instrumented logs. Owner: Ravi Menon. ETA: 2026-03-24.
- A3: Add a deploy preflight CI gate that simulates tag-filtering paths and fails fast. Owner: Marcus Liu. ETA: 2026-03-16.
- A4: Implement automated rollback trigger linked to SLO monitor (proof-of-concept to toggle feature flags automatically if p95 > threshold for 3 minutes). Owner: Priya Nandakumar. ETA: 2026-04-02.
- A5: Update runbook with explicit rollback command sequences for Dedicated pools (step-by-step). Owner: Sofia Torres. ETA: 2026-03-15.

Notes for next release window (process improvements)
- Add synthetic customers in canary that exercise long-tail prompts to surface KV-cache regressions earlier.
- Ramp plan tweak: keep a small steady-state low-traffic spine for 30 minutes post-variant-swap to measure p99 heat over time.
- Bake a “deploy dry-run” that runs the exact canary traffic script against a staging pool to validate tag filters and canary orchestration.
- Expand smoke test matrix to include quantization-mode toggles and dedicated-pool burst scenarios.

Open questions / unresolved items
- Can we implement a 'soft-fallback' where model-variant selection falls back at inference time (per-request) without a full rollback? Trade-offs: complexity vs faster mitigation. (Owner: Marcus — research spike 2d)
- Is the current autoscaling headroom for Dedicated pools sufficient for bursty rerank workloads? Need capacity simulation. (Owner: Ravi — add to next capacity runbook).

Appendix: quick command snippets (for oncall)
- rollback model variant: ./releasectl rollback --service=model-serving --variant=stable --reason="latency-spike"
- reduce rerank concurrency: ./trafficctl throttle --route=/v1/re-rank --factor=0.7
- drain dedicated pool: ./infractl drain-pool --pool=dedicated-gpu-4 --grace=60

Endnotes:
- This document should be copied into CONFLUENCE-Release-Runbook as the sprinted findings and checklist.
- Follow-ups will be tracked in JIRA-4821 and GITHUB-PR-1298.

Quick highlights for exec snippet (one-liner):
"A model-variant swap caused a transient latency and cache churn; we rolled the variant back, applied a temporary concurrency circuit-breaker, and opened five action items (kernel fix, cache hardening, CI preflight, automated rollback POC, runbook updates). No customer-facing outages reported."

"Notes to self" (informal):
- remember to capture the exact timing trace from trace-id: trace-2026-03-09-08-49 (Marcus)
- bump rerank smoke test to run on weekdays at 04:00 UTC in CI schedule
